'''''Caryota kiriwongensis,''''' also known as '''the giant caryota,''' is a palm of peninsular Thailand. It belongs to the palm family [[Palmae]] or [[Arecaceae]]. 

== Description ==
It is a recent discovery, first seen in 1992 by palmophile Aow Panya and described in 1998 by Dr. Donald Hodel. It is a very large palm; up to {{convert|36|m}} height and {{cvt|0.9|m}} DBH (diameter at breast height). It is perhaps most notable for its very large, bipinnate fronds, up to {{cvt|11|m}} total length, of which {{cvt|8|m}} is the blade or [[Lamina (leaf)|lamina]], {{cvt|50|cm}} the petiole, and {{cvt|2.5|m}} the [[crownshaft]] sheath. There are 2,500 fan-shaped or wedge-shaped  leaflets.<ref>{{ cite journal | last= Hodel | first= Donald | date= March 1998 | title= Two New Giant Caryotas...etc | journal= The Palm Journal | issue= 139 | pages= 53 & photo p. 52}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last= Hodel | first= Donald | date= December 2002 |  title= <not recorded> | journal= Palms |  volume= 53 | issue= 4 | pages= 171–172}} this is a supplementum to the description</ref>
